embedded_waveform_measurements.scope: Self-contained measurement projection of all eight reviewed boundary windows. The full local source receipt additionally retains all2120 individual10ms RMS bins; this projection preserves the directly measured quiet intervals, candidate-boundary RMS values, intervening energy counts and word contexts needed to understand each finding without private files.

method.energy: Non-overlapping 160-sample (10 ms) bins on the global 16k PCM sample grid; RMS normalized by 32768, converted to dBFS and rounded to 0.001 dB. Zero energy is displayed at -240 dBFS.
method.quiet: Contiguous bins below each of -45/-40/-35 dBFS lasting at least 50 ms. -40 dBFS is the primary diagnostic; alternatives expose threshold sensitivity.
method.service_time_formula: scene.start + event.offset / 10000000 / scene.tempo; end additionally includes event.duration. These original service boundaries generated the captions and are not an independent accuracy reference.
method.window: From one second before the earlier ASR/caption boundary to one second after the later one, limited to scene bounds then expanded by less than 10 ms to the PCM bin grid.
method.scope: Existing PCM from final MP4 decoding only. No provider calls, new ASR, waveform edits, phoneme identification or listening.

verification.recomputation: Little-endian signed 16-bit struct decoding; 10 log10 of mean square normalized by 32768 squared, compared to the original 20 log10 RMS calculation.

scenes.expected_narration: A network moves information in packets. Think of one packet as a small delivery envelope. Its header contains information used to handle the delivery. Its payload contains the carried content, which may be encrypted. A byte is a small numerical unit with values from zero to two hundred fifty five. The model can process those numbers without turning them into readable sentences. The envelope analogy is only a starting point: real packets use several protocol layers, and a payload is not guaranteed to contain a complete application message. One conversation usually spans many packets.

scenes.expected_narration: An intrusion detection system, often shortened to I D S, observes traffic and raises alerts for investigation. The neural classifier is one component that can help assign a category. Capture, flow assembly, data transformation, alert thresholds, event storage, and operational response are additional components. A prediction alone does not decide whether to block a customer connection. In this project the browser demonstration displays previously recorded predictions. That is useful for explaining behavior and mistakes, but opening the page does not connect to a network tap or execute a model inside your browser.

scenes.expected_narration: Throughout the lesson, separate three claims. Implemented means there is code intended to do a job. Executed means a recorded command actually ran. Validated means a specific check passed against a stated expectation. A script can exist without its hardware path being tested. A training job can complete without matching a published accuracy. A checksum can match without proving the dataset is unbiased. When someone says everything works, ask which activity, on which environment, with which evidence. The repository's manifests, logs, predictions, and failure records make that question answerable.

scenes.expected_narration: The authors identify three difficulties. First, some sequence models become expensive when processing many input units. Second, a traffic representation may discard useful content while keeping misleading clues, such as identifiers tied to the collection environment. Third, common categories can dominate learning while rare categories perform poorly. These are distinct problems. A faster model does not automatically fix biased input data. Adding packet timing does not automatically solve a rare class problem. The paper combines architectural, representation, and training ideas to address them. Our measurements should be interpreted against the parts actually enabled.

record.scope: Every one of 84 spoken passages transcribed independently from the actual encoded MP4. ASR can misrecognize words/numbers and does not establish human listening, pronunciation acceptance or timing acceptance.

method.alignment: Per-scene monotonic exact normalized-token blocks; SequenceMatcher autojunk=False.
method.normalization: Case/punctuation/hyphens; spoken integer/decimal expansions; valid grouped commas; percent; uppercase spelled acronym joins; Net Mamba and Smart NIC joins. Ambiguous ASR numerals remain unmatched.
method.boundary_acceptance: Exact boundary match, probability >=0.8, positive duration, original-word edge, >=3 matching tokens or unique >=4-letter token. Long sentence-onset words absorbing the preceding pause and boundaries touching a collapsed zero-duration ASR word are uncertain. Any unmatched expected/ASR interior token or untrusted edge makes the cue uncertain.
method.signed_delta: Caption minus ASR time. Positive start = late appearance; positive end = late disappearance.
method.limitations: ASR lexical confidence is not calibrated timing confidence. No human listening or +/-0.5-second human acceptance. New audio must have new hash-matched ASR. Service captions already use separate word-end and word-start boundaries; compare both independently and preserve intentional inter-word gaps. Do not infer correction from uncertain ASR.

cues.text: We also did not build a complete live intrusion detection system.

cues.text: Those limits do not erase the work.

cues.text: They tell you precisely what the work establishes and what a next

cues.chapter_title: Start here: what you built
cues.text: A network moves information in packets.

cues.chapter_title: Start here: what you built
cues.text: Think of one packet as a small delivery envelope.

cues.chapter_title: Start here: what you built
cues.text: Its header contains information used to handle the delivery.

cues.chapter_title: Start here: what you built
cues.text: Its payload contains the carried content, which may be encrypted.

cues.chapter_title: Start here: what you built
cues.text: A byte is a small numerical unit with values from zero to two

cues.chapter_title: Start here: what you built
cues.text: hundred fifty five.

cues.chapter_title: Start here: what you built
cues.text: The model can process those numbers without turning them into

cues.chapter_title: Start here: what you built
cues.text: readable sentences.

cues.chapter_title: Start here: what you built
cues.text: The envelope analogy is only a starting point: real packets use

cues.chapter_title: Start here: what you built
cues.text: several protocol layers, and a payload is not guaranteed to

cues.chapter_title: Start here: what you built
cues.text: contain a complete application message.

cues.chapter_title: Start here: what you built
cues.text: One conversation usually spans many packets.

cues.chapter_title: Start here: what you built
cues.text: A flow is a set of related packets, grouped using an explicit

cues.chapter_title: Start here: what you built
cues.text: rule.

cues.chapter_title: Start here: what you built
cues.text: A common starting point uses source and destination addresses,

cues.chapter_title: Start here: what you built
cues.text: source and destination ports, and the transport protocol.

cues.chapter_title: Start here: what you built
cues.text: Direction handling, timeouts, and packet ordering also need a

cues.chapter_title: Start here: what you built
cues.text: definition.

cues.chapter_title: Start here: what you built
cues.text: Imagine two cameras sending messages at the same time.

cues.chapter_title: Start here: what you built
cues.text: The next two captured packets could belong to different cameras.

cues.chapter_title: Start here: what you built
cues.text: Their proximity in a file does not make them one conversation.

cues.chapter_title: Start here: what you built
cues.text: This matters because Net Mamba Plus learns from a structured view

cues.chapter_title: Start here: what you built
cues.text: of a flow.

cues.chapter_title: Start here: what you built
cues.text: Supplying unrelated packet rows changes the meaning of its input.

cues.chapter_title: Start here: what you built
cues.text: An intrusion detection system, often shortened to I D S, observes

cues.chapter_title: Start here: what you built
cues.text: traffic and raises alerts for investigation.

cues.chapter_title: Start here: what you built
cues.text: The neural classifier is one component that can help assign a

cues.chapter_title: Start here: what you built
cues.text: category.

cues.chapter_title: Start here: what you built
cues.text: Capture, flow assembly, data transformation, alert thresholds,

cues.chapter_title: Start here: what you built
cues.text: event storage, and operational response are additional

cues.chapter_title: Start here: what you built
cues.text: components.

cues.chapter_title: Start here: what you built
cues.text: A prediction alone does not decide whether to block a customer

cues.chapter_title: Start here: what you built
cues.text: connection.

cues.chapter_title: Start here: what you built
cues.text: In this project the browser demonstration displays previously

cues.chapter_title: Start here: what you built
cues.text: recorded predictions.

cues.chapter_title: Start here: what you built
cues.text: That is useful for explaining behavior and mistakes, but opening

cues.chapter_title: Start here: what you built
cues.text: the page does not connect to a network tap or execute a model

cues.chapter_title: Start here: what you built
cues.text: inside your browser.

cues.chapter_title: Start here: what you built
cues.text: Throughout the lesson, separate three claims.

cues.chapter_title: Start here: what you built
cues.text: Implemented means there is code intended to do a job.

cues.chapter_title: Start here: what you built
cues.text: Executed means a recorded command actually ran.

cues.chapter_title: Start here: what you built
cues.text: Validated means a specific check passed against a stated

cues.chapter_title: Start here: what you built
cues.text: expectation.

cues.chapter_title: Start here: what you built
cues.text: A script can exist without its hardware path being tested.

cues.chapter_title: Start here: what you built
cues.text: A training job can complete without matching a published

cues.chapter_title: Start here: what you built
cues.text: accuracy.

cues.chapter_title: Start here: what you built
cues.text: A checksum can match without proving the dataset is unbiased.

cues.chapter_title: Start here: what you built
cues.text: When someone says everything works, ask which activity, on which

cues.chapter_title: Start here: what you built
cues.text: environment, with which evidence.

cues.chapter_title: Start here: what you built
cues.text: The repository's manifests, logs, predictions, and failure

cues.chapter_title: Start here: what you built
cues.text: records make that question answerable.

cues.chapter_title: Start here: what you built
cues.text: You now have the vocabulary needed for the rest of the course.

cues.text: We will use short questions to check understanding, with clearly

cues.text: The answer is no: the classifier is one tested component.

cues.chapter_title: The PDF: ideas, experiments and boundaries
cues.text: Now open the attached paper conceptually.

cues.chapter_title: The PDF: ideas, experiments and boundaries
cues.text: It is the January twenty twenty six first preprint version of Net

cues.chapter_title: The PDF: ideas, experiments and boundaries
cues.text: Mamba Plus, a framework of pretrained models for efficient and

cues.chapter_title: The PDF: ideas, experiments and boundaries
cues.text: accurate network traffic classification.

cues.chapter_title: The PDF: ideas, experiments and boundaries
cues.text: A research paper describes a problem, a proposed method,

cues.chapter_title: The PDF: ideas, experiments and boundaries
cues.text: experiments, and conclusions.

cues.chapter_title: The PDF: ideas, experiments and boundaries
cues.text: It is not an installation manual or a complete specification of

cues.chapter_title: The PDF: ideas, experiments and boundaries
cues.text: every released data file.

cues.chapter_title: The PDF: ideas, experiments and boundaries
cues.text: This paper covers several model variants and datasets.

cues.chapter_title: The PDF: ideas, experiments and boundaries
cues.text: Our repository exercises a particular multimodal Mamba classifier

cues.chapter_title: The PDF: ideas, experiments and boundaries
cues.text: and one compatible downstream dataset, so its scope is narrower.

cues.chapter_title: The PDF: ideas, experiments and boundaries
cues.text: The authors identify three difficulties.

cues.chapter_title: The PDF: ideas, experiments and boundaries
cues.text: First, some sequence models become expensive when processing many

cues.chapter_title: The PDF: ideas, experiments and boundaries
cues.text: input units.

cues.chapter_title: The PDF: ideas, experiments and boundaries
cues.text: Second, a traffic representation may discard useful content while

cues.chapter_title: The PDF: ideas, experiments and boundaries
cues.text: keeping misleading clues, such as identifiers tied to the

cues.chapter_title: The PDF: ideas, experiments and boundaries
cues.text: collection environment.

cues.chapter_title: The PDF: ideas, experiments and boundaries
cues.text: Third, common categories can dominate learning while rare

cues.chapter_title: The PDF: ideas, experiments and boundaries
cues.text: categories perform poorly.

cues.chapter_title: The PDF: ideas, experiments and boundaries
cues.text: These are distinct problems.

cues.chapter_title: The PDF: ideas, experiments and boundaries
cues.text: A faster model does not automatically fix biased input data.

cues.chapter_title: The PDF: ideas, experiments and boundaries
cues.text: Adding packet timing does not automatically solve a rare class

cues.chapter_title: The PDF: ideas, experiments and boundaries
cues.text: problem.

cues.chapter_title: The PDF: ideas, experiments and boundaries
cues.text: The paper combines architectural, representation, and training

cues.chapter_title: The PDF: ideas, experiments and boundaries
cues.text: ideas to address them.

cues.chapter_title: The PDF: ideas, experiments and boundaries
cues.text: Our measurements should be interpreted against the parts actually

cues.chapter_title: The PDF: ideas, experiments and boundaries
cues.text: enabled.

cues.chapter_title: The PDF: ideas, experiments and boundaries
cues.text: Multimodal means using several views of the same observation.

cues.chapter_title: The PDF: ideas, experiments and boundaries
cues.text: Here it means packet byte content, packet lengths, and time gaps.

cues.chapter_title: The PDF: ideas, experiments and boundaries
cues.text: Suppose two flows contain similarly encrypted bytes, but one

cues.chapter_title: The PDF: ideas, experiments and boundaries
cues.text: sends a steady series of small packets while another sends large

cues.chapter_title: The PDF: ideas, experiments and boundaries
cues.text: bursts.

cues.chapter_title: The PDF: ideas, experiments and boundaries
cues.text: Size and timing can provide additional structure.

cues.chapter_title: The PDF: ideas, experiments and boundaries
cues.text: This is an explanatory example, not a measured claim about our

cues.chapter_title: The PDF: ideas, experiments and boundaries
cues.text: test set.

cues.chapter_title: The PDF: ideas, experiments and boundaries
cues.text: The important requirement is that all three views describe the

cues.chapter_title: The PDF: ideas, experiments and boundaries
cues.text: same flow.

cues.chapter_title: The PDF: ideas, experiments and boundaries
cues.text: Combining bytes from one connection with timing from another

cues.chapter_title: The PDF: ideas, experiments and boundaries
cues.text: would create a physically inconsistent example even if the tensor

cues.chapter_title: The PDF: ideas, experiments and boundaries
cues.text: dimensions still matched.

cues.chapter_title: The PDF: ideas, experiments and boundaries
cues.text: The paper discusses Mamba and an alternative optimized

cues.chapter_title: The PDF: ideas, experiments and boundaries
cues.text: Transformer called Net Trans.

cues.chapter_title: The PDF: ideas, experiments and boundaries
cues.text: Flash Attention belongs to that alternative's attention

cues.chapter_title: The PDF: ideas, experiments and boundaries
cues.text: implementation; it is not evidence that our active Mamba

cues.chapter_title: The PDF: ideas, experiments and boundaries
cues.text: classifier uses an attention layer.

cues.chapter_title: The PDF: ideas, experiments and boundaries
cues.text: A Mamba block processes a sequence while updating numerical

cues.chapter_title: The PDF: ideas, experiments and boundaries
cues.text: state, with updates influenced by the input.

cues.chapter_title: The PDF: ideas, experiments and boundaries
cues.text: This can make sequence processing efficient.

cues.chapter_title: The PDF: ideas, experiments and boundaries
cues.text: It does not mean the software maintains a live table of network

cues.chapter_title: The PDF: ideas, experiments and boundaries
cues.text: connections between predictions.

cues.chapter_title: The PDF: ideas, experiments and boundaries
cues.text: In our tested configuration the classifier uses four Mamba

cues.chapter_title: The PDF: ideas, experiments and boundaries
cues.text: blocks.

cues.chapter_title: The PDF: ideas, experiments and boundaries
cues.text: Other branches present in a source repository are not

cues.chapter_title: The PDF: ideas, experiments and boundaries
cues.text: automatically exercised by that configuration.

cues.chapter_title: The PDF: ideas, experiments and boundaries
cues.text: For a first reading, use the framework diagram to understand the

cues.chapter_title: The PDF: ideas, experiments and boundaries
cues.text: overall path.

cues.chapter_title: The PDF: ideas, experiments and boundaries
cues.text: Then read the traffic representation section to see how raw

cues.chapter_title: The PDF: ideas, experiments and boundaries
cues.text: traffic becomes structured inputs.

cues.chapter_title: The PDF: ideas, experiments and boundaries
cues.text: The model details explain embeddings, sequence processing,

cues.chapter_title: The PDF: ideas, experiments and boundaries
cues.text: pretraining, and classification.

cues.chapter_title: The PDF: ideas, experiments and boundaries
cues.text: The online system section adds capture and shared memory around a

cues.chapter_title: The PDF: ideas, experiments and boundaries
cues.text: classifier.

cues.chapter_title: The PDF: ideas, experiments and boundaries
cues.text: The evaluation section reports dataset comparisons, efficiency,

cues.chapter_title: The PDF: ideas, experiments and boundaries
cues.text: and other experiments.

cues.chapter_title: The PDF: ideas, experiments and boundaries
cues.text: Keep a note beside each number identifying the model, task, and

cues.chapter_title: The PDF: ideas, experiments and boundaries
cues.text: machine that produced it.

cues.chapter_title: The PDF: ideas, experiments and boundaries
cues.text: This reading habit prevents a result from one experiment being

cues.chapter_title: The PDF: ideas, experiments and boundaries
cues.text: accidentally used as proof for a different system.

cues.chapter_title: The PDF: ideas, experiments and boundaries
cues.text: The paper's comparison includes a ninety seven point five percent

cues.chapter_title: The PDF: ideas, experiments and boundaries
cues.text: accuracy figure for the relevant C I C IoT twenty twenty two

cues.chapter_title: The PDF: ideas, experiments and boundaries
cues.text: result.

cues.chapter_title: The PDF: ideas, experiments and boundaries
cues.text: Our three seed mean is eighty six point six five percent.

cues.chapter_title: The PDF: ideas, experiments and boundaries
cues.text: We preserve both numbers and the differences in runtime and

cues.chapter_title: The PDF: ideas, experiments and boundaries
cues.text: training settings.

cues.chapter_title: The PDF: ideas, experiments and boundaries
cues.text: We did not isolate the cause of the gap.

cues.chapter_title: The PDF: ideas, experiments and boundaries
cues.text: The paper also studies few shot learning, unfamiliar

cues.chapter_title: The PDF: ideas, experiments and boundaries
cues.text: distributions, and a label distribution aware strategy for

cues.chapter_title: The PDF: ideas, experiments and boundaries
cues.text: imbalanced classes.

cues.chapter_title: The PDF: ideas, experiments and boundaries
cues.text: Those results do not become reproduced merely because our basic

cues.chapter_title: The PDF: ideas, experiments and boundaries
cues.text: classifier runs.

cues.chapter_title: The PDF: ideas, experiments and boundaries
cues.text: Each additional claim would need its own matching protocol,

cues.chapter_title: The PDF: ideas, experiments and boundaries
cues.text: inputs, and measured outputs.

cues.chapter_title: The PDF: ideas, experiments and boundaries
cues.text: Two details deserve special care.

cues.chapter_title: The PDF: ideas, experiments and boundaries
cues.text: A token is a numerical input unit for the sequence model; we will

cues.chapter_title: The PDF: ideas, experiments and boundaries
cues.text: build those units later.

cues.chapter_title: The PDF: ideas, experiments and boundaries
cues.text: The paper's hyperparameter table shows four hundred one tokens

cues.chapter_title: The PDF: ideas, experiments and boundaries
cues.text: for its byte representation.

cues.chapter_title: The PDF: ideas, experiments and boundaries
cues.text: Our actual multimodal classifier receives four hundred forty

cues.chapter_title: The PDF: ideas, experiments and boundaries
cues.text: three tokens, after including sizes, intervals, and three summary

cues.chapter_title: The PDF: ideas, experiments and boundaries
cues.text: tokens.

cues.chapter_title: The PDF: ideas, experiments and boundaries
cues.text: Later, the paper reports online throughput of two hundred sixty

cues.chapter_title: The PDF: ideas, experiments and boundaries
cues.text: one point eight seven megabits per second for its Net Mamba

cues.chapter_title: The PDF: ideas, experiments and boundaries
cues.text: prototype on different hardware.

cues.chapter_title: The PDF: ideas, experiments and boundaries
cues.text: That is not our measured multimodal deployment.

cues.chapter_title: The PDF: ideas, experiments and boundaries
cues.text: Before presenting any paper number, identify the exact experiment

cues.chapter_title: The PDF: ideas, experiments and boundaries
cues.text: it describes.

cues.chapter_title: The first CSV: CICIDS2017 packet records
cues.text: Next, inspect your first attached data file.

cues.chapter_title: The first CSV: CICIDS2017 packet records
cues.text: A C S V is plain text organized as rows and comma separated

cues.chapter_title: The first CSV: CICIDS2017 packet records
cues.text: fields.

cues.chapter_title: The first CSV: CICIDS2017 packet records
cues.text: A spreadsheet can display it as a table, but this file is not a

cues.chapter_title: The first CSV: CICIDS2017 packet records
cues.text: database server or a network capture program.

cues.chapter_title: The first CSV: CICIDS2017 packet records
cues.text: The full profile counted one million four hundred ten thousand

cues.chapter_title: The first CSV: CICIDS2017 packet records
cues.text: two hundred fifty five packet records in the C I C I D S

cues.chapter_title: The first CSV: CICIDS2017 packet records
cues.text: twenty seventeen file.

cues.chapter_title: The first CSV: CICIDS2017 packet records
cues.text: Each row has fifteen hundred five columns.

cues.chapter_title: The first CSV: CICIDS2017 packet records
cues.text: The stored profile lets you inspect that structure without

cues.chapter_title: The first CSV: CICIDS2017 packet records
cues.text: opening a multi gigabyte spreadsheet.

cues.chapter_title: The first CSV: CICIDS2017 packet records
cues.text: Fifteen hundred columns are named payload byte one through

cues.chapter_title: The first CSV: CICIDS2017 packet records
cues.text: payload byte fifteen hundred, using underscores in the exact

cues.chapter_title: The first CSV: CICIDS2017 packet records
cues.text: header names.

cues.chapter_title: The first CSV: CICIDS2017 packet records
cues.text: They describe payload byte positions.

cues.chapter_title: The first CSV: CICIDS2017 packet records
cues.text: Five additional columns are time to live, total length, protocol,

cues.chapter_title: The first CSV: CICIDS2017 packet records
cues.text: a delta time field, and the label.

cues.chapter_title: The first CSV: CICIDS2017 packet records
cues.text: Time to live is a protocol field limiting how far a packet can

cues.chapter_title: The first CSV: CICIDS2017 packet records
cues.text: travel; it is not a timestamp.

cues.chapter_title: The first CSV: CICIDS2017 packet records
cues.text: Total length is a recorded packet length value.

cues.chapter_title: The first CSV: CICIDS2017 packet records
cues.text: Protocol describes the communication protocol.

cues.chapter_title: The first CSV: CICIDS2017 packet records
cues.text: Delta time suggests a time difference, but the CSV alone does not

cues.chapter_title: The first CSV: CICIDS2017 packet records
cues.text: establish its units or how it was computed.

cues.chapter_title: The first CSV: CICIDS2017 packet records
cues.text: The label is the category supplied with the record.

cues.chapter_title: The first CSV: CICIDS2017 packet records
cues.text: This CSV contains fifteen label names.

cues.chapter_title: The first CSV: CICIDS2017 packet records
cues.text: The largest group is labeled benign, with three hundred sixty two

cues.chapter_title: The first CSV: CICIDS2017 packet records
cues.text: thousand one hundred eight rows.

cues.chapter_title: The first CSV: CICIDS2017 packet records
cues.text: Do S Hulk has two hundred fifty thousand, and D Do S has two

cues.chapter_title: The first CSV: CICIDS2017 packet records
cues.text: hundred forty one thousand four hundred five.

cues.chapter_title: The first CSV: CICIDS2017 packet records

cues.text: The actual experiment uses the authors' native flow files.

cues.chapter_title: Follow one native flow into the model
cues.text: Each file contains a JSON array of flow objects.

cues.chapter_title: Follow one native flow into the model
cues.text: JSON is structured text with named fields and lists.

cues.chapter_title: Follow one native flow into the model
cues.text: The data field holds a list of packet byte strings.

cues.chapter_title: Follow one native flow into the model
cues.text: Sizes and intervals are space separated numeric strings.

cues.chapter_title: Follow one native flow into the model
cues.text: Labeled examples also carry class information.

cues.chapter_title: Follow one native flow into the model
cues.text: The small example on screen is synthetic and deliberately

cues.chapter_title: Follow one native flow into the model
cues.text: shortened to explain the schema.

cues.chapter_title: Follow one native flow into the model
cues.text: It is not a recovered packet capture.

cues.chapter_title: Follow one native flow into the model
cues.text: The real loader converts these fields into fixed numerical

cues.chapter_title: Follow one native flow into the model
cues.text: arrays, so variable length flows can enter the same neural model.

cues.chapter_title: Follow one native flow into the model
cues.text: The byte branch uses the first five packets and up to three

cues.chapter_title: Follow one native flow into the model
cues.text: hundred twenty stored bytes from each.

cues.chapter_title: Follow one native flow into the model
cues.text: Five times three hundred twenty gives sixteen hundred byte

cues.chapter_title: Follow one native flow into the model
cues.text: positions.

cues.chapter_title: Follow one native flow into the model
cues.text: Short inputs receive padding and long inputs are truncated.

cues.chapter_title: Follow one native flow into the model
cues.text: The paper describes an eighty byte header allocation and a two

cues.chapter_title: Follow one native flow into the model
cues.text: hundred forty byte payload allocation per packet.

cues.chapter_title: Follow one native flow into the model
cues.text: The released stored bytes can be loaded, but their complete

cues.chapter_title: Follow one native flow into the model
cues.text: extraction history has not been independently verified.

cues.chapter_title: Follow one native flow into the model
cues.text: We therefore say stored bytes when describing what our executed

cues.chapter_title: Follow one native flow into the model
cues.text: loader actually consumed.

cues.chapter_title: Follow one native flow into the model
cues.text: This preserves the difference between a paper's intended

cues.chapter_title: Follow one native flow into the model
cues.text: representation and a release's established provenance.

cues.chapter_title: Follow one native flow into the model
cues.text: The loader scales a byte value by dividing by two hundred fifty

cues.chapter_title: Follow one native flow into the model
cues.text: five.

cues.chapter_title: Follow one native flow into the model
cues.text: It then subtracts one half and divides by one half.

cues.chapter_title: Follow one native flow into the model
cues.text: Zero becomes negative one, and two hundred fifty five becomes

cues.chapter_title: Follow one native flow into the model
cues.text: positive one.

cues.chapter_title: Follow one native flow into the model
cues.text: This puts byte inputs on a common numerical scale.

cues.chapter_title: Follow one native flow into the model
cues.text: A tensor is simply a multidimensional array of numbers.

cues.chapter_title: Follow one native flow into the model
cues.text: For a batch of flows, the byte tensor has dimensions batch, one,

cues.chapter_title: Follow one native flow into the model
cues.text: one, and sixteen hundred.

cues.chapter_title: Follow one native flow into the model
cues.text: The extra dimensions match the original model's interface.

cues.chapter_title: Follow one native flow into the model
cues.text: A matching shape is necessary for execution, but it still does

cues.chapter_title: Follow one native flow into the model
cues.text: not prove that the underlying bytes mean the right thing.

cues.chapter_title: Follow one native flow into the model
cues.text: The size branch uses the first twenty packet sizes, clipped

cues.chapter_title: Follow one native flow into the model
cues.text: between zero and fifteen hundred.

cues.chapter_title: Follow one native flow into the model
cues.text: Its padding value is clipped to the same upper limit.

cues.chapter_title: Follow one native flow into the model
cues.text: The timing branch uses the first twenty gaps and maps an observed

cues.chapter_title: Follow one native flow into the model
cues.text: gap x to one plus x divided by two plus x.

cues.chapter_title: Follow one native flow into the model
cues.text: Zero maps to one half; one maps to two thirds.

cues.text: Those are numerical examples, not an assertion about seconds.

cues.text: Missing intervals use padding that maps to one.

cues.text: The sixteen hundred byte positions are grouped into four byte

cues.chapter_title: Follow one native flow into the model
cues.text: strides, producing four hundred byte tokens.

cues.chapter_title: Follow one native flow into the model
cues.text: forty three.

cues.chapter_title: Follow one native flow into the model

cues.text: Pretraining teaches a representation from a reconstruction task.

cues.chapter_title: How pretraining, training and inference work
cues.text: Fine tuning adapts that representation to known categories using

cues.chapter_title: How pretraining, training and inference work
cues.text: labeled examples.

cues.chapter_title: How pretraining, training and inference work
cues.text: Inference uses a fixed classifier to produce scores without

cues.chapter_title: How pretraining, training and inference work
cues.text: updating its parameters.

cues.chapter_title: How pretraining, training and inference work
cues.text: A checkpoint saves model state so a later process can reload it.

cues.chapter_title: How pretraining, training and inference work
cues.text: Some training checkpoints also include optimizer state and

cues.chapter_title: How pretraining, training and inference work
cues.text: settings.

cues.chapter_title: How pretraining, training and inference work
cues.text: The word checkpoint therefore describes a file's role, not a

cues.chapter_title: How pretraining, training and inference work
cues.text: guarantee that it contains a complete deployment package.

cues.chapter_title: How pretraining, training and inference work
cues.text: During masked pretraining, parts of the input are hidden or

cues.chapter_title: How pretraining, training and inference work
cues.text: zeroed according to the original procedure.

cues.chapter_title: How pretraining, training and inference work
cues.text: A reconstruction decoder tries to recover the missing content and

cues.chapter_title: How pretraining, training and inference work
cues.text: feature values.

cues.chapter_title: How pretraining, training and inference work
cues.text: The loss measures reconstruction error.

cues.chapter_title: How pretraining, training and inference work
cues.text: The optimizer adjusts parameters to reduce that error over

cues.chapter_title: How pretraining, training and inference work
cues.text: examples.

cues.chapter_title: How pretraining, training and inference work
cues.text: Labels such as Flood or Cameras are not the reconstruction

cues.chapter_title: How pretraining, training and inference work
cues.text: target.

cues.chapter_title: How pretraining, training and inference work
cues.text: Learning a useful representation this way may help a later

cues.chapter_title: How pretraining, training and inference work
cues.text: classification task, but a falling reconstruction loss does not

cues.chapter_title: How pretraining, training and inference work
cues.text: itself prove attack detection accuracy.

cues.text: The full paper uses a much larger pretraining protocol than the

cues.text: In fine tuning, a batch contains multiple labeled flows.

cues.text: The forward pass computes category scores.

cues.text: A classification loss compares those scores with the supplied

cues.text: The backward pass computes gradients, which describe how

cues.chapter_title: How pretraining, training and inference work
cues.text: The optimizer then updates those parameters.

cues.text: Repeating this process across the training loader forms an epoch.

cues.chapter_title: How pretraining, training and inference work
cues.text: A learning rate controls the scale of updates.

def ref(path):
    return {"path": path, "sha256": V.digest(V.local(ROOT, path))}


def source_data():
    source = V.resolve_source(ROOT, V.read(V.local(ROOT, SOURCE)))
    V.require(source.get("release_tag") == "course-video-v4", "Expected the frozen v4 source")
    scenes = {s["id"]: s for c in source["chapters"] for s in c["scenes"]}
    return source, scenes


def exact_excerpt(scenes, selector):
    scene_id, begin, end = selector
    text = scenes[scene_id]["narration"]
    V.require(text.count(begin) == 1, f"Changed or ambiguous excerpt beginning: {scene_id}: {begin}")
    start = text.index(begin)
    finish = text.index(end, start) + len(end)
    result = text[start:finish]
    V.substantive(result, scene_id + " selected excerpt")
    return result


def claim_records():
    records = []
    for name, spec in SCHEMA["claims"].items():
        file, pointer = spec["file"], spec["pointer"]
        source_unit, unit = spec["source_unit"], spec["unit"]
        value = V.pointer(V.read(V.local(ROOT, file)), pointer)
        decimals = 4 if unit in {"nll", "brier"} else 2 if unit in {"percent", "percentage_points"} else 0
        records.append({"id": name, "evidence": ref(file), "pointer": pointer,
                        "source_unit": source_unit, "unit": unit, "decimals": decimals,
                        "expected": V.convert_quantity(value, source_unit, unit, decimals)})
    return records


def inspect_source():
    """Check existing source attribution/excerpts without declaring a review passed."""
    source, scenes = source_data()
    records = claim_records()
    V.check_claims(ROOT, {"claims": records}, source, scenes, version=VERSION)
    return {"status": "source_and_schema_inspected", "readiness": False,
            "source": ref(SOURCE), "schema": SCHEMA,
            "claims": records, "source_claim_bindings": source["claims"],
            "cluster_excerpts": {name: {field: exact_excerpt(scenes, selector)
                for field, selector in selectors.items()} for name, selectors in EXCERPTS.items()},
            "paper": paper_mappings(),
            "limit": "Deterministic extraction and attribution checks only; actual content, visual and media reviews remain required."}


def paper_mappings():
    text = (ROOT / PAPER_GUIDE).read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    body = V.section(text, PAPER_ANCHOR)
    descriptions = {}
    for line in body.splitlines():
        if not line.startswith("|"):
            continue
        cells = [c.strip() for c in line.strip().strip("|").split("|")]
        if len(cells) == 3:
            descriptions[cells[0]] = cells[2]
    prefixes = {"abstract": "Abstract and I.", "I": "Abstract and I.", "II": "II.", "III": "III.",
                "IV": "IV.", "V": "V.", "VI": "VI.", "VII": "VII.", "VIII-A": "VIII-A.",
                "VIII-B": "VIII-B–C.", "VIII-C": "VIII-B–C.", "VIII-D": "VIII-D–F.",
                "VIII-E": "VIII-D–F.", "VIII-F": "VIII-D–F.", "VIII-G": "VIII-G–H.",
                "VIII-H": "VIII-G–H.", "VIII-I": "VIII-I–J.", "VIII-J": "VIII-I–J.", "IX": "IX."}
    rows = []
    for section_id in V.PAPER_SECTIONS:
        matches = [value for label, value in descriptions.items() if label.startswith(prefixes[section_id])]
        V.require(len(matches) == 1, f"Missing or ambiguous paper roadmap row: {section_id}")
        V.substantive(matches[0], "paper " + section_id)
        rows.append({"id": section_id, "scene_ids": ["paper-05"], "companion_anchor": PAPER_ANCHOR,
                     "depth": "companion", "explanation": matches[0]})
    return {"version": "2601.21792v1", "guide": ref(PAPER_GUIDE), "sections": rows}


def inventory_anchors(paths):
    guide = ROOT / GUIDE
    text = guide.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    anchors = re.findall(r'<a\s+(?:id|name)=["\'](file-[^"\']+)["\'][^>]*>', text)
    matches = {path: [] for path in paths}
    for anchor in anchors:
        body = V.section(text, anchor)
        # The entry's first repository file link is its subject. Later links may
        # describe relationships and must not become alternative file coverage.
        for angled, plain in re.findall(r"\]\((?:<([^>]+)>|([^\s)]+))(?:\s+[^)]*)?\)", body):
            value = unquote(angled or plain).split("#", 1)[0]
            if urlsplit(value).scheme:
                continue
            target = (guide.parent / value).resolve()
            if target.is_file() and target.is_relative_to(ROOT):
                path = target.relative_to(ROOT).as_posix()
                if path in matches:
                    matches[path].append(anchor)
                break
    bad = [path for path, values in matches.items() if len(values) != 1]
    V.require(not bad, "Missing/ambiguous file companion anchors: " + ", ".join(bad[:12]))
    return {path: values[0] for path, values in matches.items()}


def file_scene(path, scene_ids):
    special = {"repro.py": "code-02", "evaluate.py": "code-03", "predict.py": "code-04", "replay.py": "code-05",
               "calibration.py": "code-04", "tools/calibrate.py": "code-04",

               V.CSV: "cic-csv-06", V.NATIVE: "unsw-csv-05", V.RESULTS: "results-01", V.PORTABILITY: "setup-05"}
    if path in special:
        return special[path]
    if "/frames/" in path and Path(path).stem in scene_ids:
        return Path(path).stem
    if path.startswith("configs/"):
        return "code-06"
    if path.startswith("requirements/"):
        return "setup-04"
    if path.startswith(".github/"):
        return "setup-03"
    if path.startswith("tests/"):
        return "repository-05"
    if path.startswith("tools/"):
        name = Path(path).stem
        if name in {"build_cuda", "build_gb10", "capture_runtime"}:
            return "setup-04"
        if name in {"check_gpu_runtime", "check_model_runtime"}:
            return "setup-05"
        if name == "profile_csvs":
            return "cic-csv-06"
        if name == "benchmark":
            return "hardware-01"
        if name == "probe_export":
            return "hardware-03"
        if name == "review_experiments":
            return "results-05"
        if any(word in name for word in ("video", "course", "narrate", "package", "guide", "replay")):
            return "repository-04"
        return "repository-03"
    if path.startswith("docs/customer/demo/video/"):
        return "repository-06"
    if "docs/customer/demo/" in path:
        return "demo-01"
    if path.startswith("docs/customer/evidence/calibration/"):
        return "results-07"
    if "/evidence/" in path or "/audit-evidence/" in path:
        return "repository-05"
    return "repository-02" if "/" not in path else "repository-05"

               "claims": claim_records(), "reviews": reviews,
               "checks": {}, "known_material_defects": [],
               "assembly": {"review_bundle": ref(review_path),
                            "method": "Exact reviewed source/guide excerpts and existing completed proof records; no status was synthesized.",
                            "inventory_scope": "Every Git-tracked and nonignored file is mapped; no published files are excluded.",
                            "local_only_inputs_scope": "Historical production-workspace observations outside the published inventory; these directories are not required in a consumer clone.",
                            "local_only_inputs": actual_local_only_inputs(paths)}}
    for kind in V.REQUIRED_CHECKS:
        supplied = bundle.get("checks", {}).get(kind)
        if supplied is not None:
            V.artifact(ROOT, supplied, kind + " completed check")
            records["checks"][kind] = copy.deepcopy(supplied)
            continue
        path = f"{CHECK_DIRECTORY}/{kind}.json"
        if (ROOT / path).is_file():
            records["checks"][kind] = ref(path)
        else:
            V.require(content_only, f"Missing actual required {kind} check record")
    # No publishable candidate is returned until the same verifier accepts it.
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="v4-coverage-validation-", dir=ROOT / "runs/video-course") as directory:
        pending = Path(directory) / "candidate.json"
        pending.write_bytes(V.canonical(records))
        result = V.verify_coverage(ROOT, coverage_path=pending.relative_to(ROOT).as_posix(),
                                   manifest_path=manifest_path, source_path=SOURCE, inventory=paths, content_only=content_only, version=VERSION)
    return records, result


def ignored_output(path):
    value = (ROOT / path).resolve()
    V.require(value.is_relative_to(ROOT / "runs/video-course"), "This helper only writes ignored runs/video-course outputs")
    V.require(value.relative_to(ROOT / "runs/video-course").parts[0].startswith("v4"), "Use a v4-named helper output; historical outputs are protected")
    V.require(not value.exists(), "Use a fresh helper output path")
    value.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    return value


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--inspect", action="store_true", help="Inspect existing source claims/excerpts; never propose source edits or claim readiness")
    parser.add_argument("--reviews", default=REVIEW_BUNDLE)
    parser.add_argument("--manifest", default=MANIFEST)
    parser.add_argument("--content", action="store_true", help="Require completed content review; do not claim media readiness")
    parser.add_argument("--output", required=True, help="Fresh path below ignored runs/video-course")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    try:
        output = ignored_output(args.output)
        if args.inspect:
            record, receipt = inspect_source(), {"status": "inspection_only", "source_edited": False, "readiness": False}
        else:
            record, receipt = assemble(args.reviews, args.manifest, args.content)
        output.write_text(json.dumps(record, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
        print(json.dumps({"output": output.relative_to(ROOT).as_posix(), "sha256": V.digest(output), "verification": receipt}, indent=2))
        return 0
    except (ValueError, KeyError, TypeError, IndexError, OSError) as exc:
        print(json.dumps({"status": "failed", "error": str(exc), "coverage_written": False}))
        return 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

"""Local v4 audit identities and output guards; no review status is inferred."""
import hashlib
import json
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
SOURCE = ROOT / 'docs/customer/video-course-v4-source.json'
PUBLIC = ROOT / 'docs/customer/demo/video/v4'
MANIFEST = PUBLIC / 'media-manifest.json'
WORK = ROOT / 'runs/video-course/v4-neural'
FFMPEG = '/home/nvidia/learn/_video/bin/ffmpeg'
FFPROBE = '/home/nvidia/learn/_video/bin/ffprobe'


def require(condition, message):
    if not condition:
        raise ValueError(message)


def sha(path):
    hasher = hashlib.sha256()
    with Path(path).open('rb') as stream:
        for chunk in iter(lambda: stream.read(1024 * 1024), b''):
            hasher.update(chunk)
    return hasher.hexdigest()


def relative(path):
    return Path(path).resolve().relative_to(ROOT).as_posix()


def ref(path):
    return {'path': relative(path), 'sha256': sha(path)}


def local_run_path(path):
    value = (ROOT / path).resolve()
    base = ROOT / 'runs/video-course'
    require(value.is_relative_to(base), 'Audit cache/output must be below this worktree runs/video-course')
    parts = value.relative_to(base).parts
    require(parts and parts[0].startswith('v4'), 'Use v4-named cache/output paths; v3 is protected')
    return value


def new_output(path):
    value = local_run_path(path)
    value.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=False)
    return value


def write(path, document):
    with Path(path).open('x', encoding='utf-8') as stream:
        stream.write(json.dumps(document, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False, allow_nan=False) + '\n')


def load_manifest(path=MANIFEST):
    path = (ROOT / path).resolve()
    raw = path.read_bytes()
    manifest = json.loads(raw)
    require(manifest.get('release_tag') == 'course-video-v4', 'Expected v4 media')
    require(manifest.get('source_sha256') == sha(SOURCE), 'Media source is not the current v4 source')
    name = manifest['media_name']
    require(Path(name).name == name and name.endswith('.mp4'), 'Invalid v4 MP4 name')
    for name in (name, 'captions.vtt'):
        identity = manifest['artifacts'][name]
        file = PUBLIC / name
        require(file.is_file() and sha(file) == identity['sha256'] and file.stat().st_size == identity['bytes'],
                'Missing or stale v4 media artifact: ' + name)
    return manifest, raw


def unchanged(manifest_path, original_bytes, manifest):
    require((ROOT / manifest_path).resolve().read_bytes() == original_bytes, 'Manifest changed during audit')
    load_manifest(manifest_path)


def receipt(manifest, raw):
    return {'completed_at': datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
            'source_sha256': manifest['source_sha256'],
            'manifest_sha256': hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest(),
            'mp4_sha256': sha(PUBLIC / manifest['media_name']),
            'vtt_sha256': sha(PUBLIC / 'captions.vtt'),
            'artifacts': [ref(PUBLIC / manifest['media_name']), ref(PUBLIC / 'captions.vtt')]}

"""Check all current v4 evidence claims and every serialized VTT/SRT cue."""
import argparse
import html
import json
import re
from pathlib import Path
import assemble_v4_coverage as A
import v4_audit_common as C


def stamp(value):
    hours, minutes, seconds = value.replace(',', '.').split(':')
    return int(hours) * 3600 + int(minutes) * 60 + float(seconds)


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument('--manifest', type=Path, default=C.MANIFEST)
    parser.add_argument('--output', type=Path, default=C.ROOT / 'runs/video-course/v4-final-claims-captions')
    args = parser.parse_args()
    args.manifest = (C.ROOT / args.manifest).resolve()
    output = None
    try:
        manifest, raw = C.load_manifest(args.manifest)
        source, scenes = A.source_data()
        records = A.claim_records()
        bindings = A.V.check_claims(C.ROOT, {'claims': records}, source, scenes, version=4)
        A.V.check_captions(C.ROOT, manifest, C.PUBLIC.relative_to(C.ROOT), scenes, bindings)
        output = C.new_output(args.output)
        (output / 'manifest-input.json').write_bytes(raw)
        srt = C.PUBLIC / 'captions.srt'
        C.require(C.sha(srt) == manifest['artifacts'][srt.name]['sha256'], 'Stale SRT identity')
        blocks = srt.read_text().strip().split('\n\n')
        C.require(len(blocks) == len(manifest['caption_cues']), 'SRT cue count differs')
        for index, (block, cue) in enumerate(zip(blocks, manifest['caption_cues']), 1):
            lines = block.splitlines()
            C.require(len(lines) >= 3 and lines[0] == str(index), 'Incorrect SRT index or text')
            C.require(re.fullmatch(r'\d{2,}:[0-5]\d:[0-5]\d,\d{3} --> \d{2,}:[0-5]\d:[0-5]\d,\d{3}', lines[1]), 'Malformed SRT timestamp')
            start, end = map(stamp, lines[1].split(' --> '))
            C.require(abs(start - cue['start']) <= .002 and abs(end - cue['end']) <= .002, 'SRT timing differs')
            C.require(A.V.normalized(html.unescape(' '.join(lines[2:]))) == A.V.normalized(cue['text']), 'SRT text differs')
        quantities = [{**record, **bindings[record['id']], 'status': 'passed',
                       'actual_stored_quantity': A.V.pointer(A.V.read(C.ROOT / record['evidence']['path']), record['pointer'])}
                      for record in records]
        C.unchanged(args.manifest, raw, manifest)
        result = {**C.receipt(manifest, raw), 'status': 'passed',
                  'method': f'Recomputed {len(records)} schema-required evidence quantities with units/rounding and exact scene attribution; parsed every final VTT/SRT cue against source and measured windows.',
                  'quantities': quantities, 'caption_count': len(blocks),
                  'spoken_scenes_with_complete_caption_text': sum(bool(s['narration']) for s in scenes.values()),
                  'practice_scenes': sum(s['kind'] == 'pause' for s in scenes.values()),
                  'srt_sha256': C.sha(srt), 'maximum_timestamp_serialization_error_seconds': .002,
                  'manifest_snapshot': C.ref(output / 'manifest-input.json'),
                  'scope': 'Deterministic text, evidence and serialized timing checks. Semantic content, encoded speech, visual placement and human listening require separate reviews.',
                  'known_material_defects': []}
        C.write(output / 'receipt.json', result)
        print(json.dumps({'status': 'passed', 'claims': len(records), 'caption_count': len(blocks), 'output': C.relative(output)}))
        return 0
    except (OSError, ValueError, KeyError, TypeError, IndexError) as error:
        failure = {'status': 'failed', 'error': str(error), 'readiness': False}
        if output is not None:
            C.write(output / 'failure.json', failure)
        print(json.dumps(failure))
        return 1


if __name__ == '__main__':
    raise SystemExit(main())

"""Compare exact-index final v4 MP4 frames with PNGs, timed ASS and clip composites.

This is an encoded-pixel comparison, not a visual-comprehension review.
"""
import argparse
import json
import re
import subprocess
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
from pathlib import Path
from PIL import Image, ImageChops, ImageStat
import v4_audit_common as C


def sample_requests(manifest):
    fps = manifest['fps']
    requests = []
    by_id = {s['id']: s for s in manifest['scenes']}
    for scene in manifest['scenes']:
        requests.extend([(scene['id'] + '-middle', (scene['start'] + scene['end']) / 2),
                         (scene['id'] + '-first-frame', scene['start'])])
    offsets = {'orientation-04': [1.3, 2.6, 4.3, 6, 8], 'features-02': [1, 7, 16, 27],
               'features-05': [1.3, 2.6, 4.3, 6], 'learning-04': [4, 12, 22, 32],
               'results-01': [1, 8, 14, 19, 26, 33], 'results-07': [1, 8, 16, 24],
               'demo-05': [1, 8, 16, 24], 'demo-06': [1, 8, 16, 24],
               'setup-02': [3, 8, 15, 22, 29]}
    for name, values in offsets.items():
        scene = by_id[name]
        for offset in values:
            if scene['start'] + offset < scene['end']:
                requests.append((name + '-motion-' + str(offset), scene['start'] + offset))
    for scene in manifest['scenes']:
        clip = scene.get('motion_clip')
        if clip:
            first = round((scene['start'] + clip['start_seconds']) * fps)
            stop = first + round(clip['duration_seconds'] * fps)
            for name, index in [('before', first - 1), ('first', first), ('middle', (first + stop) // 2), ('last', stop - 1), ('after', stop)]:
                C.require(scene['start'] <= index / fps < scene['end'], 'Clip boundary falls outside its scene')
                requests.append((scene['id'] + '-clip-' + name, index / fps))
    requests.extend((c['id'] + '-preceding-frame', c['start'] - 1 / fps) for c in manifest['chapters'][1:])
    requests.append(('last-frame', manifest['scheduled_seconds'] - 1 / fps))
    # Retain aliases when two semantic checks select the same decoded frame.
    selected = {}
    for name, seconds in requests:
        index = round(seconds * fps)
        entry = selected.setdefault(index, {'names': [], 'requested_seconds': []})
        entry['names'].append(name)
        entry['requested_seconds'].append(seconds)
    return selected


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument('--manifest', type=Path, default=C.MANIFEST)
    parser.add_argument('--work', type=Path, default=C.WORK)
    parser.add_argument('--output', type=Path, default=C.ROOT / 'runs/video-course/v4-final-frames')
    parser.add_argument('--ffmpeg', default=C.FFMPEG)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    args.manifest = (C.ROOT / args.manifest).resolve()
    output = None
    try:
        manifest, raw = C.load_manifest(args.manifest)
        work = C.local_run_path(args.work)
        ass = work / 'captions.ass'
        C.require(ass.is_file(), 'Final timed ASS production cache is required for pixel comparison')
        output = C.new_output(args.output)
        (output / 'manifest-input.json').write_bytes(raw)
        (output / 'captions-input.ass').write_bytes(ass.read_bytes())
        fps = manifest['fps']
        media = C.PUBLIC / manifest['media_name']
        requests = sample_requests(manifest)
        ordered = sorted(requests)
        selection = '+'.join(f'eq(n,{index})' for index in ordered)
        command = [args.ffmpeg, '-hide_banner', '-nostats', '-xerror', '-threads', '8', '-i', str(media),
                   '-vf', f"settb=1/{fps},select='{selection}',showinfo", '-fps_mode', 'vfr',
                   '-frames:v', str(len(ordered)), '-threads', '2', str(output / 'actual-%03d.png')]
        process = subprocess.run(command, capture_output=True, text=True)
        (output / 'extract.log').write_text(process.stderr)
        process.check_returncode()
        pts = [int(x) for x in re.findall(r' n:\s*\d+\s+pts:\s*(\d+)\s+pts_time:', process.stderr)]
        C.require(pts == ordered, 'Decoded frame indices/PTS differ from requested frames')

        def check(pair):
            number, index = pair
            seconds = index / fps
            scene = next(s for s in manifest['scenes'] if s['start'] <= seconds < s['end'])
            actual, expected = output / f'actual-{number:03d}.png', output / f'expected-{number:03d}.png'
            frame = (C.ROOT / scene['visuals'][0]['path']).resolve()
            C.require(frame.is_relative_to(C.PUBLIC) and C.sha(frame) == scene['visuals'][0]['sha256'], 'Stale or non-v4 frame')
            base = frame
            if scene.get('motion_clip'):
                first = round((scene['start'] + scene['motion_clip']['start_seconds']) * fps)
                count = round(scene['motion_clip']['duration_seconds'] * fps)
                if first <= index < first + count:
                    base = work / 'motion-frames' / scene['id'] / f'composite-{index - first + 1:04d}.png'
            subprocess.run([args.ffmpeg, '-v', 'error', '-threads', '1', '-framerate', str(fps), '-i', str(base),
                            '-vf', f'setpts=PTS+{index},ass={output / "captions-input.ass"}',
                            '-frames:v', '1', '-threads', '1', str(expected)], check=True)
            with Image.open(actual) as image:
                left = image.convert('RGB')
            with Image.open(expected) as image:
                right = image.convert('RGB')
            C.require(left.size == right.size == (1920, 1080), 'Unexpected frame dimensions')
            diff = ImageChops.difference(left, right)
            metrics = {name: sum(ImageStat.Stat(diff.crop(box)).mean) / 3 for name, box in [
                ('full_frame_mae', (0, 0, 1920, 1080)), ('upper_850_mae', (0, 0, 1920, 850)),
                ('caption_footer_mae', (0, 850, 1920, 1080))]}
            return {'name': requests[index]['names'][0], **requests[index], 'scene': scene['id'],
                    'frame_index': index, 'timestamp_numerator': index, 'timestamp_denominator': fps,
                    'actual_frame_time': seconds, **metrics, 'within_limit': all(v <= 3 for v in metrics.values()),
                    'actual_png': C.relative(actual), 'actual_sha256': C.sha(actual),
                    'expected_png': C.relative(expected), 'expected_sha256': C.sha(expected), 'base_png_sha256': C.sha(base),
                    'visible_cues': [cue['text'] for cue in manifest['caption_cues'] if cue['start'] <= seconds < cue['end']]}

        with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=3) as pool:
            records = list(pool.map(check, enumerate(ordered, 1)))
        C.unchanged(args.manifest, raw, manifest)
        result = {**C.receipt(manifest, raw), 'status': 'passed' if all(r['within_limit'] for r in records) else 'failed',
                  'frames': records, 'command': command, 'limit_mean_absolute_rgb_difference': 3,
                  'ass_sha256': C.sha(output / 'captions-input.ass'), 'manifest_snapshot': C.ref(output / 'manifest-input.json'),
                  'scope': 'Every scene start/midpoint, chapter boundary, selected motion states, and actual recorded-clip boundaries compared by decoded frame index against source PNG/composite plus timed ASS. Complete decode and semantic visual review are separate; no human full watch is claimed.'}
        C.write(output / 'frame-check.json', result)
        print(json.dumps({'status': result['status'], 'frames': len(records), 'failures': [r['names'] for r in records if not r['within_limit']]}))
        return 0 if result['status'] == 'passed' else 1
    except (OSError, ValueError, KeyError, TypeError, StopIteration, subprocess.CalledProcessError) as error:
        failure = {'status': 'failed', 'error': str(error), 'readiness': False}
        if output is not None:
            C.write(output / 'failure.json', failure)
        print(json.dumps(failure))
        return 1


if __name__ == '__main__':
    raise SystemExit(main())
